chunks: Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a man who purchased a female slave, and she remained with him for months without menstruating, and this was not due to old age, and women stated that she was not pregnant. He asked: is it permissible that she be approached in the private part?
So he said: “Menstruation may be held back by wind without pregnancy, so there is no harm in touching her in the private part.”

key_terms.الرِّيحُ: wind; here, a bodily cause said to delay menstruation
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is intercourse permissible with a slave woman whose menstruation has stopped but who is not pregnant?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a female slave whose menstruation was delayed without being due to old age or pregnancy. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that absence of menstruation can occur for reasons other than pregnancy, so intercourse is not prohibited on that basis alone.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.199 - Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) was asked about a man who purchased a female slave who stayed with him for months without menstruating, and this was not due to age, and it was mentioned by women that She was not pregnant.
He asked whether it was permissible to have intercourse with her in this state.
Imam (as) said: "The lack of menstruation may sometimes be caused by a blockage of wind, not necessarily due to pregnancy. Therefore, there is no problem in engaging with her in that way."
